severity.summary: Critically ill: advanced HIV (CD4 9) with fever, confusion, hyponatraemia and borderline blood pressure. Sepsis-3 septic shock criteria cannot be assessed without lactate and vasopressor status.

leadingDiagnosis.name: Disseminated fungal infection (probable histoplasmosis) with secondary HLH
leadingDiagnosis.rationale: Skin papules, pancytopenia, ferritin 18000 and CD4 9 with failure of empirical TB treatment; no tissue or culture confirmation yet.

differential.name: Disseminated tuberculosis
evidenceAgainst: GeneXpert and urine LAM negative, which do not exclude TB at this CD4

mustNotMiss.name: Cryptococcal meningitis
mustNotMiss.howToExclude: serum CrAg and lumbar puncture with CSF CrAg

bedsideStat.test: Blood cultures including mycobacterial and fungal bottles

first24h.test: Lumbar puncture with CSF CrAg, culture and Xpert if safe

definitive.test: Bone marrow aspirate and trephine with culture and histology
Skin smear and biopsy of papules for histology and fungal culture

immediate.action: Liposomal amphotericin B preferred over deoxycholate formulation because of raised creatinine; monitor creatinine, potassium and magnesium daily
Correct hyponatraemia cautiously and give empirical hydrocortisone if cortisol is low or the patient deteriorates

targeted.action: Haematology referral for HLH management and trigger-directed therapy

supportive.action: Cautious IV fluids with sodium monitoring

existingTreatmentDecisions.reason: negative GeneXpert and LAM do not exclude TB at CD4 9; stop only if an alternative diagnosis is proven and TB is excluded on culture

timingDecisions.recommendation: Defer ART until cryptococcal meningitis is excluded and amphotericin has been started; then start within the timeframe in the SA HIV Clinicians Society guideline
timingDecisions.reason: risk of IRIS and unmasked CNS disease

questionAnswers.question: Should we continue TB treatment?
questionAnswers.answer: Yes, continue for now, because the negative tests do not exclude TB at this CD4; revisit when culture and marrow results are back.

questionAnswers.question: When should ART be started?
questionAnswers.answer: Not before cryptococcal meningitis is excluded and antifungal therapy is under way; then early, per the SA HIV Clinicians Society guideline.
